messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that has been confirmed so far is the exoplanet **HD 100546 b**. It orbits the young star HD 100546 and has a radius of roughly **2.5 × Jupiter’s radius** (about 180,000 km). This makes it larger than any planet in our own Solar System—Jupiter’s radius is only about 71,500 km. 

There are other very large candidates, such as HD 106906 b (≈ 11 R_J) and some “super‑Jupiters” that may exceed 10 R_J, but their status as bona fide planets is still under investigation. As of now, HD 100546 b is the most massive and largest planet that has been reliably measured.
